topic: There is a hole in your vision right now. Find it with one eye closed.
title: The Hole In Your Vision
idea: Every eye has a spot with no light sensors where the optic nerve leaves, and your brain paints over it so you never notice.
hook: Is there a hole in your vision right now?

beats.line: Let's find it, so close your left eye.
With your right eye, stare at the cross on the left.
Now slowly bring your phone closer, then back.
At one spot, the red dot on the right simply vanishes.
That's your blind spot, where your optic nerve leaves the eye.
About one point two million nerve fibers exit there, with zero light sensors.
The gap could hide more than ten full moons.
You never notice because your brain paints over it with whatever is around.

end.line: There's a hole in your vision right now, and your brain hides it.

description: Close your left eye and stare at the cross. The red dot disappears. That's the hole in your vision your brain hides from you.

facts.claim: At the optic nerve head (optic disc) there are no photoreceptors, only nerve fibers; this is the physiologic blind spot, about 15 degrees temporal to fixation and about 7.5 degrees across.
facts.source: University of Iowa EyeRounds visual field tutorial https://webeye.ophth.uiowa.edu/eyeforum/tutorials/VF-testing/

facts.claim: Approximately 1.2 million nerve fibers make up each human optic nerve (on screen: ABOUT 1,200,000 NERVE FIBERS).
facts.source: University of Iowa glaucoma guide https://webeye.ophth.uiowa.edu/eyeforum/books/glaucoma_guide/chapter1.html (OK-number in FACTS-batch-047-050.md)

facts.claim: With one eye closed and staring at a mark, a dot at the side disappears at a certain distance; the brain fills in the missing information.
facts.source: Neuroscience for Kids, University of Washington https://faculty.washington.edu/chudler/chvision.html

facts.claim: The full Moon is about half a degree wide, so a 5.5 to 7.5 degree blind spot spans more than ten Moon widths (on screen: 10+ FULL MOONS, 11 moons drawn).
facts.source: NASA https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/moon/the-moon-illusion-why-does-the-moon-look-so-big-sometimes/ + Iowa EyeRounds (own calculation, see FACTS-batch-047-050.md)

facts.claim: The only thing the viewer is asked to do is close one eye and move the phone; no fixed vanishing distance is stated.
facts.source: Safety and wording rules for 048 in FACTS-batch-047-050.md

factcheck.note: Spoken numbers (one point two million, zero, more than ten) and on-screen numbers (1,200,000, 0, 10+) match the 048 OK list in FACTS-batch-047-050.md. No fixed vanishing distance, the hole is not called central, and fifteen moons is never said. Test layout for the right eye: cross left, dot right, dot never animated.
